A center, Adams has played for four NBA teams since making his NBA debut in 2013. After playing one season with the [[Wellington Saints]] in New Zealand in 2011, Adams moved to the United States in 2012 to play [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. He played for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Panthers]] for one season and was then selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] with the 12th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. Following the 2013–14 season, Adams was named to [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]]. In November 2020, after seven years in Oklahoma City, Adams was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. In August 2021, he was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], where he played until being traded to the Rockets in 2024. Adams is known for his physical strength. == Early life == Steven Adams was born in [[Rotorua]], New Zealand. His father, Sid Adams, was from [[Bristol]], England and served in the [[Royal Navy]].{{cite web |last=Saker |first=John |title=The Adams family: born to run |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/dominion-post/capital-life/9723642/The-Adams-family-born-to-run |work=Stuff |access-date=11 September 2023 |date=16 February 2014}} His mother, Lilika Ngauamo, was a nurse from the South Pacific island of [[Tonga]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/nba/steven-adams-family-lifestyle/|title=Who Are Steven Adams' Parents? All About the Rockets Center's Personal Life and Family|website=profootballnetwork.com|date=3 May 2025}} Adams is biracial. Sid Adams stood {{convert|2.11|m|ftin}} tall.{{cite web|last=Fittipaldo|first=Ray|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2012/10/07/Pitt-big-man-Steven-Adams-backstory-is-as-interesting-as-his-future-is-intriguing/stories/201210070252|title=Pitt big man Steven Adams' backstory is as interesting as his future is intriguing|work=Post-Gazette.com|date=7 October 2012|access-date=11 December 2012}} Two of Adams' half-sisters are athletes: Dame [[Valerie Adams]] is a dual Olympic gold medallist and four-time world champion [[Shot put|shot-putter]] and [[Lisa Adams (athlete)|Lisa Adams]] is a para athlete who has won gold at the Paralympics in shot-put.{{Cite web|title=Lisa Adams – Athletics {{!}} Paralympic Athlete Profile|url=https://www.paralympic.org/lisa-adams|access-date=28 August 2021|work=International Paralympic Committee}} His brothers, Warren and Sid Jr., had careers in the New Zealand [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|National Basketball League]].{{cite web|last=Hinton|first=Marc|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/4398036/Teenager-Adams-tipped-for-basketball-big-time|title=Teenager Adams tipped for basketball big time|work=Stuff.co.nz|date=28 November 2010|access-date=14 February 2018}}{{cite web|last=Heagney|first=George|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/manawatu-standard/sport/9326636/Te-Hunas-team-ready-to-bounce|title=Te Huna's team ready to bounce|work=Stuff.co.nz|date=25 October 2013|access-date=14 February 2018}} Adams' sister, Gabriella Adams-Gavet, has played basketball for the [[New Zealand women's national basketball team|New Zealand national team]].{{cite web |last=McFadden |first=Suzanne |title=Adams family proud of their Tall Fern sister |url=https://www.newsroom.co.nz/lockerroom/adams-family-proud-of-their-tall-fern-sister |website=Newsroom |access-date=11 September 2023 |date=27 December 2022}} Sid Adams fathered a large number of children. Some sources indicate that he had 18 children by five different women,{{Cite web|url=https://heavy.com/sports/2016/05/steven-adams-family-basketball-thunder-parents-father-mother-sisters-brothers-siblings-nationality-height-tall/|title=Steven Adams' Family: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know|first=Craig|last=Bennett|date=18 May 2016|website=Heavy Sports}} another states that he had 18 children by six different women,{{Cite web|url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/nba-active-basketball-news-who-are-steven-adams-parents-inside-houston-rockets-stars-life-shared-with-seventeen-siblings/|title=Who Are Steven Adams’ Parents? Inside Rockets Star’s Life Shared With 17 Siblings|website=Essentially Sports|first=Meenu|last=Tomy|date=6 January 2025}} and other reports say he fathered 21 children by six different women. In Steven Adams's autobiography, ''My Life, My Fight'' (2018), he wrote, "'No one knows for sure how many kids my dad had. If you ask anyone in the media they’ll say he had 18, or maybe even 20, but they won’t know where that number came from. If you ask my sister Viv, she’ll say it's 16. I always thought there were 14 of us. Whatever the number, there will only ever be one Sid Adams'". Lilika Ngauamo died of cancer in 2000. Sid Adams died of stomach cancer in 2007, when Adams was 13. Adams has identified his father's death as one of the defining events of his life. In a 2012 interview, Adams recalled:
When I lost my dad, that was a big hit for me. I didn't have that parental guidance, and I kind of took advantage of it because I was a stupid idiot. I decided not to go to school a couple of times, go when I felt like it. I always lied to my brothers and sisters. They'd ask: 'Are you going to school?' I'd say 'yeah'. They eventually found out.
After his father died, Adams left high school and joined a gang known as the [[Mongrel Mob]].{{Cite web|url=https://heavy.com/sports/2019/04/steven-adams-nationality-ethnicity-background/|title=Steven Adams Nationality, Ethnicity & Background|first=Sam|last=Dodge|date=17 April 2019|website=Heavy Sports}} Blossom Cameron rescued Adams from the streets of Rotorua and took him to [[Wellington]].{{cite web|url=http://pittsburghpanthers.com/news/2011/11/11/Steven_Adams_Bio.aspx|title=Steven Adams Bio|website=PittsburghPanthers.com|date=11 November 2011 |access-date=14 February 2018}} Cameron took responsibility for Adams and introduced him to Wellington basketball coach [[Kenny McFadden]]. McFadden accepted Adams into his basketball academy, and Blossom Cameron enrolled him in [[Scots College, Wellington|Scots College]]. The only rule McFadden had for Adams was that he had to attend school every day if he wanted to play basketball. While there was pressure for Adams to turn professional straight out of high school because it was believed he would never be able to qualify for the [[NCAA]], Adams did well at Scots College and passed through the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] Clearinghouse after graduating from Scots in December 2011. ==Preparatory school and college== After graduating from Scots College in December 2011, Adams enrolled at [[Notre Dame Preparatory School (Fitchburg, Massachusetts)|Notre Dame Preparatory School]], a basketball prep school in [[Fitchburg, Massachusetts]], for one semester. It was arranged so that he could acclimate himself to American basketball before enrolling at [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]] in June 2012. In his lone season at Pittsburgh, Adams was named the [[Big East]] Preseason Rookie of the Year and earned Big East All-Rookie Team honours.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/players/steven/adams/203500|title=Steven Adams stats, details, videos, and news|website=NBA.com|access-date=14 February 2018}} He started all 32 games during the [[2012–13 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|2012–13 season]] and averaged 7.2 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 2.0 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=http://pittsburghpanthers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=427|title=2012–13 Men's Basketball Roster – Steven Adams|website=PittsburghPanthers.com|access-date=14 February 2018}} Following the season, Adams declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web|last=Grimes|first=Tim|title=NBA Draft 2013: Steven Adams Declares, and Is an Underrated Prospect|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1591224-nba-draft-2013-steven-adams-declares-and-is-an-underrated-prospect|work=Bleacher Report|date=3 April 2013|access-date=24 June 2014}}{{cite web|last=Abercrombie|first=Nicola|title=Kiwi Steven Adams declares for NBA draft|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/8503912/Kiwi-Steven-Adams-declares-for-NBA-draft|website=Stuff.co.nz|date=3 April 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130615110344/http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/8503912/Kiwi-Steven-Adams-declares-for-NBA-draft|archive-date=15 June 2013}} ==Professional career== ===Wellington Saints (2011)=== In 2011, Adams played for the [[Wellington Saints]] of the [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|National Basketball League]].{{cite web|last=Worthington|first=Sam|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/4623859/One-size-20-step-to-Saints-giant-leap-for-NBA|title=One size-20 step to Saints, giant leap for NBA|website=Stuff.co.nz|date=9 February 2011|access-date=14 February 2018}} He went unpaid by the Saints in order to keep his college eligibility. Adams was named the New Zealand [[New Zealand NBL Rookie of the Year Award|NBL Rookie of the Year]] and helped the Saints win the championship. In 15 games for the Saints, he averaged 5.5 points and 4.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&client=11-8336-114272-159868-15173978&pID=192372016|title=Player statistics for Steven Adams|work=SportsTG.com|access-date=14 February 2018}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2013–2020)=== ====2013–16: Early years==== [[File:Kevin Seraphin Steven Adams.jpg|thumb|Adams (right) with the Thunder in February 2014, contesting with [[Kevin Séraphin]] of the [[Washington Wizards]]]] On 27 June 2013, Adams was selected with the 12th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], becoming just the second New Zealander to be selected in the NBA draft and the first New Zealander to be selected in the first round. He also became the first player out of Pittsburgh to be selected in the first round since [[1999 NBA draft|1999]] when [[Vonteego Cummings]] was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 26th overall pick.{{cite web|last=Golliver|first=Ben|url=http://nba.si.com/2013/06/27/steven-adams-nba-draft-2013/|title=Steven Adams selected No. 12 by Thunder in NBA draft|work=SI.com|date=27 June 2013|access-date=27 June 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130701033442/http://nba.si.com/2013/06/27/steven-adams-nba-draft-2013/|archive-date=1 July 2013}} On 12 July, Adams signed his rookie scale contract with the Thunder.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/adams_roberson_130712|title=Thunder Signs Steven Adams and Andre Roberson|work=NBA.com|date=12 July 2013|access-date=4 August 2013}} In his NBA debut on 30 October 2013, Adams recorded two points, three rebounds, one assist and three fouls in 18½ minutes off the bench during a 101–98 victory over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/adamsst01/gamelog/2014/ |title=Steven Adams 2013–14 Game Log |work=basketball-reference.com |access-date=14 February 2018}} Nine days later, in just his fifth NBA game, Adams recorded 17 points and 10 rebounds in a 119–110 victory over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |url=http://newsok.com/okc-thunder-steven-adams-shines-again-as-thunder-trims-pistons/article/3902858 |title=OKC Thunder: Steven Adams shines again as Thunder trims Pistons |work=NewsOK.com |date=8 November 2013 |access-date=14 December 2013}} He failed to surpass either mark for the rest of the regular season. Adams appeared in 81 games (20 starts) and averaged 3.3 points, 4.1 rebounds (ninth among NBA rookies) and 0.7 blocks (ninth among NBA rookies) in 14.8 minutes. In Game 6 of the Thunder's second-round playoff series against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], Adams recorded 10 points and a season-high 11 rebounds. The Thunder reached the [[Western Conference Finals]], where they were defeated by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in six games. At the conclusion of the 2013–14 season, Adams earned [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] honours.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_adams_140522|title=Steven Adams Named to All-Rookie Second Team|work=NBA.com|date=22 May 2014|access-date=27 May 2014}} On 16 November 2014, Adams recorded a career-high six blocks in a 69–65 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141116/HOUOKC/gameinfo.html |title=Harden leads Rockets past Thunder |work=NBA.com |date=16 November 2014 |access-date=16 November 2014}} On 25 December, he recorded a season-high 16 points and a then-career-high 15 rebounds in a 114–106 victory over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141225/OKCSAS/gameinfo.html |title=Westbrook scores 34, lifts Thunder over Spurs |work=NBA.com |date=25 December 2014 |access-date=25 December 2014}} On 21 January 2015, Adams recorded a career-high 20 rebounds in a 105–103 overtime win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150121/OKCWAS/gameinfo.html|title=KD2DC game yields Thunder win, 105–103 over Wizards in OT|work=NBA.com|date=21 January 2015|access-date=23 January 2015}} He missed 11 straight games over February and March with a broken ring finger on his right hand.{{cite web |last=Young |first=Royce |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/12300075 |title=Steven Adams has surgery |work=ESPN.com |date=9 February 2015 |access-date=26 March 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/adamsst01/gamelog/2015/|title=Steven Adams 2014–15 Game Log|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=14 February 2018}} Adams scored a season-high 16 points three times during the 2014–15 season. On 10 January 2016, Adams tied his career high of 17 points in a 115–110 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/75797826/steven-adams-equals-careerhigh-with-17-points-as-oklahoma-city-thunder-fall-to-portland |title=Steven Adams equals career-high with 17 points as Oklahoma City Thunder fall to Portland |work=Stuff.co.nz |date=11 January 2016 |access-date=11 January 2016}} On 12 April, in the regular-season finale, Adams had another 17-point performance in a 102–98 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |date=12 April 2016 |title=Leonard scores 26, helps Spurs beat Thunder in OT, 102-98 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400829102 |access-date=22 October 2023 |work=ESPN.com}}{{cite web|last=Twort|first=Matt|url=http://nzhoops.co.nz/steven-adams-bossing-chur/|title=Steven Adams Ties Career-High|work=NZhoops.co.nz|date=13 April 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20160520161249/http://nzhoops.co.nz/steven-adams-bossing-chur/|archive-date=20 May 2016}} In Game 2 of the Thunder's second-round playoff series against the Spurs, Adams recorded 12 points and 17 rebounds in the narrow 98–97 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/adamsst01/gamelog/2016/|title=Steven Adams 2015–16 Game Log|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=14 February 2018}} Six days later in Game 4, he scored 16 points as the Thunder won 111–97. Adams helped the Thunder advance to the Western Conference Finals for the second time in three years, where, in Game 1 against the [[Golden State Warriors]], he recorded 16 points and 12 rebounds in the 108–102 victory. In Game 3, Adams was kicked in the [[testes]] by [[Draymond Green]],{{cite web | url=https://fadeawayworld.net/nba-media/steven-adams-on-getting-kicked-in-the-groin-by-draymond-green-the-pain-on-that-one-mate-was-the-worst-the-absolute-worst | title=Steven Adams on Getting Kicked in the Groin by Draymond Green: "The Pain on That One Mate, Was the Worst, the Absolute Worst..." | date=13 February 2021 }} who maintained that the kick was inadvertent. Despite going up 3–1 in the series, the Thunder were defeated in seven games. ==== 2016–20: Increase in production ==== On 31 October 2016, Adams signed a four-year, $100 million contract extension with the Thunder.{{cite web |date=22 October 2023 |title=Thunder Signs Adams, Oladipo to Multi-Year Contract Extensions |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/extensions-161031 |access-date=31 October 2016 |work=NBA.com}}{{cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=31 October 2016 |title=Sources: Steven Adams finalizing $100M extension with Thunder |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources-steven-adams-progressing-toward-100m-extension-with-thunder-183853351.html |access-date=31 October 2016 |work=Yahoo.com}} On 22 November, he scored a career-high 20 points in a 111–109 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|last=Gallo|first=Nick|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/recap-lakers-161122|title=Thunder at Los Angeles Lakers Game Recap – Nov. 22, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=22 November 2016|access-date=23 November 2016}}{{cite web|last=Hinton|first=Marc|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/86806943/steve-adams-gets-careerhigh-20-points-but-la-lakers-steal-back-win|title=Steve Adams gets career-high 20 points, but LA Lakers steal back win|work=Stuff.co.nz|date=23 November 2016|access-date=23 November 2016}} Adams surpassed that mark on 9 December, scoring 24 points in a 102–99 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]]. His 17 points in the first half were a career high for a half.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899783|title=Rockets overcome Westbrook's 7th straight triple-double|work=ESPN.com|date=9 December 2016|access-date=10 December 2016}} On 1 December 2017, Adams scored a career-high 27 points on perfect shooting from the field and the free throw line to help the Thunder beat the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] 111–107.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975075|title=George, Adams lead Thunder past Timberwolves 111–107|work=ESPN.com|date=1 December 2017|access-date=2 December 2017}} On 2 February 2018, he had 23 points and 12 rebounds in a 114–100 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], reaching 3,000 career points. Adams joined [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Serge Ibaka]] as the only Thunder players with at least 3,000 career points and 350 career blocks.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975518|title=Davis' 43 points lead Pelicans past Thunder 114–100|work=ESPN.com|date=2 February 2018|access-date=2 February 2018}} On 13 February, Adams rebounds, during a 116–110 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401360728|title = Grizzlies vs. Bulls – Game Recap – February 26, 2022 – ESPN}} On 2 October 2022, Adams signed a two-year, $25.2 million contract extension with the Grizzlies.{{cite web |date=2 October 2022 |title=Grizzlies sign Steven Adams to multi-year extension |url=https://www.nba.com/news/grizzlies-sign-steven-adams-to-multi-year-extension |access-date=22 October 2023 |work=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=1 October 2022 |title=Memphis Grizzlies, Steven Adams agree to two-year, $25.2 million extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34703954 |access-date=9 March 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On 18 January 2023, he scored a game-winning tip-in to defeat the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], 115–114.{{cite web|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/basketball/giddey-stars-as-okc-equal-franchise-record-c-9496579|title=Basketball: Kiwi Steven Adams tips home NBA game winner for Memphis Grizzlies against Cleveland Cavaliers|work=[[Newshub]]|last=Chapman|first=Grant|date=January 19, 2023|access-date=January 19, 2023}} Four days later, Adams suffered a right knee injury during a 112–110 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |title=Paul returns, Suns hold on for 112-110 win over Grizzlies |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468858 |access-date=March 9, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On 24 January, the Grizzlies announced that he was diagnosed with a [[posterior cruciate ligament]] (PCL) sprain in his right knee and would be sidelined for three-to-five weeks.{{cite tweet|author=Grizzlies PR|user=GrizzliesPR|number=1618088847816142849|title=The @memgrizz announced the following medical update:|date=January 24, 2023|access-date=March 9, 2023}} On 9 March, the Grizzlies announced that Adams had received a [[Stem-cell therapy|stem cell]] injection the day before and would be re-evaluated in four weeks, ending his regular-season run.{{cite tweet|author=Grizzlies PR|user=GrizzliesPR|number=1633845102702645248|title=The @memgrizz announced the following medical update:|date=March 9, 2023|access-date=March 9, 2023}} Adams' ongoing recovery caused him to miss the playoffs; the second-seeded Grizzlies were eliminated by the seventh-seeded Lakers in the first round in six games. Adams missed the entire [[2023–24 NBA season]] as he underwent surgery on his PCL, which had not responded to non-operative rehabilitation.{{Cite web |date=22 October 2023 |title=Grizzlies' Steven Adams to undergo knee surgery, miss season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/38718289 |access-date=22 October 2023 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} ===Houston Rockets (2024–present)=== On 1 February 2024, Adams was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Victor Oladipo]] and three future second-round picks.{{cite web|first=Hiren|last=Joshi|title=Rockets Complete Trade with Memphis|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-trade-with-memphis|website=NBA.com|date=1 February 2024|access-date=2 February 2024}} On 28 October, Adams made his Rockets debut, putting up six points and three rebounds in 14 minutes off the bench in a 106–101 victory over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |title=Rockets' Steven Adams: Plays backup role in season debut |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-steven-adams-plays-backup-role-in-season-debut/amp/ |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=www.cbssports.com}} On 5 January 2025, after fully recovering from PCL surgery, Adams recorded a near [[double-double]] with eight points, nine rebounds, an assist, a block, and a steal in 17 minutes of action off the bench in a 119–115 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |date=2025-01-06 |title=Rockets' Steven Adams: Plays well in 17 minutes |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-steven-adams-plays-well-in-17-minutes/ |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=CBSSports.com}} On 22 January, Adams recorded three points, a season-high 11 rebounds, two assists, and two blocks in 19 minutes off the bench in a narrow 109–108 victory against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |date=2025-01-23 |title=Rockets' Steven Adams: Season-high 11 rebounds in win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-steven-adams-season-high-11-rebounds-in-win/ |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=CBSSports.com}} Eight days later, Adams made his first start of the season, recording a double-double with 11 points, 10 rebounds, and three assists in a narrow 120–119 loss to his former team, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web |last=Kiemen |first=Joe |date=2025-01-31 |title=Steven Adams Achieves Double-Double with 11 Points and 10 Rebounds in Rockets' Narrow Loss to Grizzlies on January 30, 2025 |url=https://knupsports.com/steven-adams-achieves-double-double-with-11-points-and-10-rebounds-in-rockets-narrow-loss-to-grizzlies-on-january-30-2025/ |access-date=2025-01-31 |work=Knup Sports}} On 2 May 2025, during the first round of the playoffs, Adams recorded 17 points, five rebounds and three blocks in a 115–107 Game 6 victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |title=Fred VanVleet and the Rockets force a deciding Game 7 by beating the Warriors 115-107 in Game 6 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401767913 |access-date=May 5, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}} The Rockets went on to lose the series in seven games. On 18 June 2025, the Rockets signed Adams to a three-year, $39 million contract extension.{{cite web|title=Rockets Sign Steven Adams to Contract Extension|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-steven-adams-to-contract-extension|website=NBA.com|date=June 18, 2025|access-date=June 21, 2025}} He made 32 appearances (11 starts) for Houston during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 5.8 points, 8.6 rebounds, and 1.5 assists. Adams suffered an ankle injury during an 18 January 2026 game against the [[2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]]; he later underwent season-ending surgery to address the malady on 28 January.{{Cite web|title=Rockets' Steven Adams has season-ending ankle surgery|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47757557/sources-rockets-steven-adams-season-ending-surgery|access-date=February 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==Player profile== Adams is known as an elite offensive rebounder{{Cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/steven-adams-effect-rockets-open-161403934.html|title=Steven Adams effect? Rockets open 2025-26 season on historic offensive rebounding pace|first=Ben|last=DuBose|date=12 November 2025|website=Yahoo Sports}} and a skilled interior defender.{{Cite web|url=https://heavy.com/sports/nba/houston-rockets/rockets-putting-together-fearsome-defensive-unit/|title=Rockets Putting Together Fearsome Defensive Unit|first=Mark|last=Deeks|date=25 July 2025|website=Heavy Sports}} He is widely considered the strongest man in the NBA.{{Cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/steven-adams-says-chopping-wood-202600334.html|title=Steven Adams says chopping wood helped him become the NBA's strongest player: "That was just normal chores"|first=Shane |last=Acedera|date=18 December 2025|website=Yahoo Sports}} Adams is generally well respected for his sense of humour, down-to-earth personality, and humility.{{Citation |title=Wild Steven Adams Stories You Don't Want To Miss {{!}} JJJ & PG | date=8 June 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kKjBsplp7rs |access-date=2023-09-02 |language=en}} On 14 December 2018, playing against the [[Denver Nuggets]], he received praise for catching his opponent [[Mason Plumlee]] after Plumlee jumped to contest a layup and fell over Adams. Despite having an uncontested shot, Adams chose to drop the ball and catch Plumlee, preventing a serious injury.{{cite web | last=Cwik | first=Chris | title=Steven Adams passes up easy points to save Mason Plumlee from a hard fall | website=Yahoo Sports | date=2018-12-15 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/steven-adams-passes-easy-layup-save-mason-plumlee-hard-fall-185630112.html |
